title: 99th Oscars: 104 films enter the international feature race
body_md:
The international feature competition at the 99th Academy Awards has attracted a record 104 contenders, according to a report published on November 26, 2026. The field brings together established auteurs, emerging directors, festival prizewinners and documentaries, offering a broad picture of contemporary filmmaking beyond the mainstream Hollywood awards conversation.

Among the entries of particular interest to audiences following Iranian cinema is Midday Meal, directed by Majid Majidi. The social drama follows Solan, a temporary teacher working in a remote Iranian village affected by drought. When the death of a benefactor threatens the school's meal program, he searches for a way to continue feeding his pupils. The report states that the film won the top prize at the Busan International Film Festival, qualifying it for consideration.

Pegah Ahangarani's documentary Rehearsals for a Revolution also appears in the coverage. Drawing on family photographs, recordings and other personal archival material, the filmmaker examines more than four decades of Iranian political history. The documentary received the Golden Eye award at Cannes. The appearance of both films in the international feature coverage should not be confused with confirmation that both are official national submissions from Iran.

Other prominent titles include Fjord, Cristian Mungiu's drama starring Renate Reinsve and Sebastian Stan as members of a family facing intervention by child protection authorities in Norway. The report identifies the film as a Palme d'Or winner and a leading awards contender. Lee Chang-dong's Possible Love, which received the Silver Lion Grand Jury Prize in Venice, explores the relationship between artistic representation, labor and human dignity.

Paweł Pawlikowski's Fatherland follows German writer Thomas Mann on a journey through postwar Germany, with Sandra Hüller appearing as his daughter Erika. Hüller also features in Rose, while İlker Çatak's Yellow Letters adds another politically engaged drama to the field.

The competition includes important milestones for countries with less established Oscar submission histories. Cyprus and Rwanda are represented by their first international feature contenders, according to the report. Their participation highlights the widening geographical scope of a category that can introduce international audiences to filmmakers whose work might otherwise receive limited distribution.

The breadth of the field is also reflected in its subjects, ranging from migration and historical memory to family relationships, economic insecurity and personal identity. Festival recognition offers useful context for audiences exploring these films, but it does not guarantee Academy recognition.

The 104 contenders are not 104 Oscar nominees. Further selection stages will determine the shortlist and eventual nominees, making this announcement the beginning of the competition rather than its final result.
